newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian must restructure first - minister.
newsitem.headline: Canadian must restructure first - minister.

text.p: Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson said on Thursday the restructuring of Canadian Airlines Corp must come before any possible consideration of aid to the troubled airline.
"Without the success of a restructuring plan, there would be no point in offering a loan or guarantee or anything else," Anderson said when asked by reporters about possible aid to the airline.
He suggested the employees of Canadian Airlines should agree to company requests to help the airline.

"We realize it is a difficult decision for the employees, but we want Mr. (Canadian Airlines chief executive Kevin) Benson's plan to succeed because otherwise the future of Canadian Airlines is very bleak."
Benson has asked for a 10 percent wage cut from employees and concessions from AMR Corp, parent of America Airlines.

Anderson repeated that the government was not considering easing restrictions on foreign ownership of Canadian carriers. Asked if he supported a merger with Air Canada, Anderson said: "We do not think there should be only one monopoly airline in Canada."
He rejected a suggestion by one of the airline's unions, the Canadian Auto Workers, to return to regulation of pricing, routes and new entrants into the markets.
